newsitem.title: FRANCE: Polisario criticises Morocco on Western Sahara.
newsitem.headline: Polisario criticises Morocco on Western Sahara.

text.p: The Polisario Front, seeking independence in the Western Sahara, said Morocco's decision to hold local elections in the territory was a "provocative action" unhelpful to the U.N.'s latest diplomatic drive.
The Polisario envoy to Algiers, Salek Youcef Boubih, quoted on Wednesday by Algerian official media as speaking after a four-day visit to the region by U.N. envoy James Baker, added:
"Morocco moved up another step in its intransigent policy instead of helping to find a solution and building a climate of confidence."
Last week former U.S. Secretary of State Baker visited Morocco, Algeria, Mauritania and the Polisario's main rear base in the Algerian southwestern area of Tindouf.
During his stay in Tindouf, the Polisario leaders announced they were releasing 85 Moroccan prisoners of war.

"The decision taken by Morocco to include occupied zones in the Western Sahara in the upcoming elections is a provocative action coming when we were expecting that Morocco will make a gesture to encourage Baker's mission as the Front did," the Polisario envoy said.

Morocco, which controls most of the Western Sahara, is to hold local council elections throughout the kingdom and in the disputed territory on June 13. The local councils will later elect representatives to about 80 percent of seats in a new upper house of parliament being set up under constitutional reforms agreed last September.
The Polisario and Morocco, who fought for 15 years, are observing a ceasefire brokered by the United Nations which has been in effect since September 1991.
But a U.N. peace plan calling for a referendum on the status of the former Spanish colony has been stalled since 1992 amid a continuing dispute over who is eligible to vote.

"I am convinced that the people in this region are overly weary with this issue and this problem and are ready for a just, lasting and definitive solution," Baker said at the end of his trip on Sunday.
